merger_description:
The transaction concerns the acquisition by Brookfield Corporation (together with funds managed and/or advised by Brookfield Corporation and/or its affiliates, **Brookfield**) through Aurora Aus Bidco Pty Ltd (**Bidco**) of 100% of the issued shares in Reliance Worldwide Corporation Limited (**RWC**) (the **Acquisition**).

Bidco is a special purpose vehicle established by Brookfield for the purpose of the Acquisition.

Brookfield is a global investment firm that deploys capital globally for investors across its core businesses, including its asset management business and its operating businesses. Brookfield is a public company, co-listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and the Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX).

RWC is an Australian publicly listed company (ASX: RWC) which designs, manufactures and supplies plumbing and heating products and solutions for residential and commercial projects. Established in Brisbane, RWC supplies its products globally and specialises in valves, fittings, connectors and water management technologies. RWC’s portfolio includes several brands, such as SharkBite, John Guest, Holman, TubeFit and others.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between Brookfield (and its
connected entities) and RWC in the supply of plumbing and
heating products and solutions for residential and
commercial projects in Australia
b. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
effects resulting from exclusionary conduct post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
